records.text: Owens said Cooper Brown was neither a Turning Point USA employee nor a UVU or Turning Point USA student and had instead been brought in as a volunteer.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So they were just doing what they were told. Well, then it's kind of interesting. You should know, but I then determined that the person doing the shoving is first and foremost not a Turning Point USA employee. He is beyond that not a student at UVU. He is not a Turning Point USA student therefore either. He was actually brought in as a volunteer, which I found to be quite strange.

verification.notes: Fox identified Cooper Brown as a Leadership Institute volunteer at the event, and the Leadership Institute's own staff profile identifies Brown as its employee and a Southern New Hampshire University graduate. Together these sources support that he was serving as a volunteer rather than as a TPUSA employee or UVU student.

records.text: Cooper Brown said he worked for the Leadership Institute, which worked hand-in-hand with conservative coalition groups on college campuses, including Turning Point USA.
records.speaker: Cooper Brown

appearances.snippet: Yeah, so this requires a little bit of background knowledge. So I work for an organization called Leadership Institute. And what we do is we work hand-in-hand with all the different conservative coalition groups on college campuses: the Young Americans for Liberty, the Students for Life, and the Turning Point USAs.

verification.notes: The original Fox interview contains Brown's identification as a Leadership Institute worker and event volunteer; the Leadership Institute independently identifies him as its staff member. The transcript accurately preserves his description of working with campus conservative groups, including Turning Point USA.
